title: UK repossessions decline but affordability concerns persist
summary:
Mortgage repossessions in the UK fell 14% year-on-year in the second quarter, with buy-to-let properties seeing a 20% decline. Industry professionals warn that affordability pressures persist despite the positive data, particularly as borrowers face refinancing onto higher interest rates.

title: Air conditioning searches double as heat influences buyers
summary:
Searches for UK homes with air conditioning have more than doubled this summer as rising temperatures influence property purchasing decisions. Data from Rightmove shows searches increased by 104% compared with the same period last year, with 87% of buyers considering cooling capacity important.

title: CentreMove enters crowded conveyancing technology market
summary:
CentreMove has launched as a new conveyancing platform, entering a competitive market of technology firms attempting to address delays in property transactions. The company, founded by Wayne Quin and solicitors Jen and Gordon Sewell, is onboarding its first estate agency client.

title: Consumer confidence rises but housing market slowdown deepens
summary:
The GfK Consumer Confidence Index rose to -17 in July from -23 in June, though property market data shows agreed sales running 9% below last year. The disconnect highlights ongoing challenges in the housing sector despite improved consumer sentiment.

title: Glasgow properties sell in 11 days as market speeds vary
summary:
Properties in Glasgow are selling in an average of 11 days, three times faster than the national average of 30 days, according to new data from property management software provider Alto. Worcester and Belfast also rank among the cities with the quickest property sales, while Wakefield recorded the slowest times.

title: Supreme Court to hear landlord appeal on gas safety rules
summary:
A landlord has been granted leave to appeal to the Supreme Court in a case that could affect thousands of ongoing possession proceedings. The dispute centres on whether Section 21 notices can be invalidated due to missing Gas Safety Certificates from before such requirements became law.

title: Tenancy fraud exposes UK rental sector to £4.1bn losses
summary:
Fraudulent tenancy applications could be exposing the UK's private rented sector to up to £4.1 billion in annual financial losses, according to analysis of over one million tenant references. Referee-flagged fraud has risen 78% year-on-year, with London recording rates twice the national average.

title: Savills reports 9% revenue growth despite UK slowdown
summary:
International property agency Savills has reported a 9% increase in group revenue for the first half of the year, with growth recorded across all business divisions. The results contrast with broader challenges facing estate agencies, though UK market activity slowed in the second quarter following geopolitical tensions and anticipated political change.

title: Rayner faces scrutiny over £20k Propertymark speaking fee
summary:
Angela Rayner has faced criticism following her acceptance of a £20,000 speaking fee from Propertymark, prompting questions about the government's stance on rent controls. The London Renters Union staged a protest outside the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.

title: Letting agents urged to assess landlord profitability
summary:
Letting agents are being advised to evaluate landlord clients based on profitability rather than portfolio size, as regulatory pressures and operational costs reshape the sector's economics. Industry analysis shows that 'cost to serve' metrics and client quality directly impact both current profitability and future business sale values.
